events.title: GitLab first released
events.summary: Dmitriy Zaporozhets created GitLab on October 8, 2011 — an open-source Git forge with issues, merge requests, and CI built in.
events.about: GitLab bundles Git hosting, code review, issue tracking, and DevOps pipelines in one Rails application — self-hosted or on GitLab.com. It became the main open-source alternative to GitHub, especially for enterprises wanting on-prem control. Example: push to a protected branch, open a merge request, and run CI jobs before merge.

narrative.whyChosen: GitLab proved a full DevOps platform could ship as open-source, not just Git hosting.
narrative.whyImportant: It gave teams a GitHub alternative with built-in CI/[CD] and self-hosting from day one.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams wanted Git collaboration without depending on a single proprietary SaaS forge.

events.title: Andrew Ng's Stanford ML course goes online
events.summary: Andrew Ng's free online [Machine Learning] course ran from October 10 to December 16, 2011 with over 100,000 enrollees — predating Coursera (which launched in 2012).
events.about: Ng's MOOCs democratized ML education before ChatGPT — training practitioners who later built recommendation, vision, and [NLP] products. He also led Google Brain and Baidu AI Lab.

narrative.whyChosen: Ng's courses created the first mass audience of practicing ML engineers.
narrative.whyImportant: MOOCs bridged academia and industry hiring pipelines for data science.
narrative.problemSolved: ML knowledge was locked in PhD programs and elite research labs.

events.title: Dart language unveiled at GOTO
events.summary: Google unveiled Dart on October 10, 2011 at GOTO Aarhus — a structured web language compiling to JavaScript or a VM.
events.about: Dart targets Flutter mobile/desktop apps, web via dart2js, and server-side tooling. Optional typing, sound null safety (2.0), and async/await made it Google's answer to large-scale client code. Flutter's widget framework made Dart the language behind many cross-platform apps.

narrative.whyChosen: Dart + Flutter became Google's cross-platform [UI] stack rivaling React Native.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed a language could target both JS engines and a native VM for structured large web apps.
narrative.problemSolved: JavaScript lacked optional types and tooling for million-line web clients; Google wanted a structured alternative.

events.title: iPhone 4S released
events.summary: Apple released the iPhone 4S on October 14, 2011 — introducing Siri and the A5 chip in the iPhone 4 body.
events.about: Siri brought voice-driven assistants to mainstream smartphones and gave developers a speech [API] path through iOS integration. The 4S also shipped an 8 MP camera that raised mobile photography expectations for app developers building camera workflows.

narrative.whyChosen: The 4S launched Siri — the assistant that pushed every platform to add voice interfaces.
narrative.whyImportant: Voice control and better cameras expanded what mobile apps could assume about device capabilities.
narrative.problemSolved: Smartphones lacked credible on-device voice assistants integrated with third-party services.

events.title: Samsung Galaxy Note released
events.summary: Samsung released the Samsung Galaxy Note — 5.3-inch display and S Pen stylus created the phablet category.
events.about: The Galaxy Note targeted stylus power users on [Android]. 5.3-inch display and s pen stylus created the phablet category. Note apps and split-screen [Android] development often targeted this hardware class.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy Note advanced Samsung's stylus phablet line.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy Note hardware defined large-screen [Android] productivity for years.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] lacked a premium large-screen stylus flagship for note-taking workflows.
